text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambia press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Supreme Court has refused to grant indemnity from prosecution to six witnesses in an electoral petition who had admitted to voting twice.
- Forest Equipment Industries, which lost business following the application of sanctions against Burundi, says the war in Zaire is hurting its export volume further.
- Zambia's tobacco output is poised for growth this year following the formation of a new tobacco marketing company, Zambezi Lead Tobacco company.
- - President Frederick Chiluba appoints a seven-man commission of inquiry to investigate the causes behind repeated student disturbances at the country's two universities.
- A women's group says youths in rural areas are forced into early marriages because they have nothing else to do.
- The ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy says it will penalise members who shows signs of wanting to succeed incumbent president Frederick Chiluba.
